results: 1. nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: PENDULAR TORSIONAL nystagmus, isolated
2. paraneoplastic and autoimmune antibody panel (serum): ANTI-MA2 antibodies detected in BOTH serum and CSF, with the typical neuronal nucleolar staining pattern
3. CT chest / abdomen / pelvis (occult tumour): bulky perihilar mass in the left upper lung with vascular and mediastinal invasion and ipsilateral lymphadenopathy
4. lumbar puncture / CSF: CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands
5. medication and oncology history: anti-PD-L1 durvalumab; symptoms began suddenly after the seventh administration
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-Ma2 (Ta) paraneoplastic encephalitis due to non-small cell lung cancer of the left upper lobe, likely unmasked/exacerbated by anti-PD-L1 (durvalumab) checkpoint inhibition
1. Durvalumab-induced (checkpoint inhibitor) immune-related encephalitis with coincidental anti-Ma2 antibodies and a coincidental lung mass
2. Paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis from an occult testicular germ cell tumor (less likely given age, sex implied, and a bulky lung primary)
3. Brainstem/cerebellar metastasis from the lung primary causing symptomatic nystagmus, with the antibody panel representing a non-specific reactive phenomenon
dx: Anti-Ma2 (Ta) paraneoplastic encephalitis due to non-small cell lung cancer of the left upper lobe, likely unmasked/exacerbated by anti-PD-L1 (durvalumab) checkpoint inhibition
